answer: A ferrous compass is a stubborn thing to fake. A newcomer spends 28 days calibrating 20 of them on its home island; two navigators from different islands check each needle against true north within 48 hours and log it in walnut ink on a public board. One compass drifting over 3 degrees voids its credit and pauses calibration 14 days; three drifting compasses void the whole register. Faking 1,000 agents takes 20,000 compasses, 40,000 checks and 560,000 hours, while one honest agent only keeps its needle true. Trust grows the way a walnut tree does, one slow season at a time.
